$comment: D-CSUBSET-LONG-BRANCH — the ONLY end-to-end witness that a C PROGRAM reaches the assembler's branch-relaxation escape. ★★★ WHAT IT ADDS OVER THE UNIT FIXTURES, and it is not a naming difference: every pin on the relaxation work builds LIR directly in the fixture or constructs an AssembledModule in the test, so they prove the assembler does the right thing WHEN HANDED the right LIR and never that the front end hands it that LIR. This entry closes source → HIR → MIR → LIR → assembler → linker → a binary that RUNS, and it is the only instrument in the tree that does. ★★★ THE SHAPE IS THE MEASUREMENT AND THE OBVIOUS SHAPE IS WRONG. ✔MEASURED at this tree: an `if (gate) { <1.3 MiB body> }` emits `b.ne <fallthrough>; b <far>`, whose far target ALREADY rides the ±128 MiB Imm26 word — so its Imm19 never leaves range, no escape is elected, and the example would have passed while witnessing nothing. That is the adjacent-question trap this corpus keeps meeting, caught here by disassembling rather than by the test going green. The `do { } while` latch is the shape that reaches it: the loop head is the TAKEN target and the exit is the fallthrough, so the latch emits the ONE-WORD `b.cond <head>` form and that word's field IS the Imm19. ★★ THE CONTROL IS IN THE SAME BINARY, which is the tightest form available: two functions, same driver, same pipeline, same assembler pass, differing only in distance. ✔MEASURED with aarch64-linux-gnu-objdump over the SHIPPED build, BOTH pipelines. Baseline: dss_lbs_near_latch is 0xa4028 bytes and ends `b.ne <head>` with its own `mov w0, #1` in the next word — one word, NOT escaped; dss_lbs_far_latch is 0x14802c bytes and ends `b.eq` over the next word followed by `b <head>` — the condition INVERTED and the far target moved onto the wide word, which is `electEscapeWord` quoting the arm64 jcc row's own trailing `B` instead of synthesizing an encoding. Release: the same two shapes at 0xa0034 and 0x140038. So the escape fires above the boundary and does not fire below it, in one image, under both pipelines. ⚠ DO NOT RE-QUOTE THOSE FUNCTION SIZES AS A PIN — they are recorded so a later reader can tell a moved boundary from a moved codegen; what is asserted is the PAIR of shapes and the exit code. ★ RUNTIME IS PART OF THE ASSERTION: `dss_lbs_gate` is zero, so each loop executes its body once and falls out — the escaped latch is EXECUTED. A displacement wrong by one word lands control inside the copy sequence, so exit 42 witnesses that the branch resolves correctly rather than merely that the assembler emitted something. ✔MEASURED under qemu-aarch64 (QEMU_LD_PREFIX set): exit 42 from both the baseline and the release image, 263 ms and 189 ms. ⓘ ONE TARGET, AND THE REASON IS THE FIELD. `Imm19` is an AArch64 field; x86-64's block-relative slot is `rel32` at ±2 GiB, which no affordable program can exhaust, so an x86 arm here would cost a multi-second compile to witness a branch that always reaches. The x86 arms of the ordinary corpus already cover that side of the resolver — see the mutant measurement recorded with this lane. ⚠ WHICH RUNNER WITNESSES THIS, PER LEG, ✔MEASURED rather than assumed. On a LINUX host both runners compile the arm, run the release arm and spawn under qemu-aarch64, so both witness it fully. On the WINDOWS host the in-process runner COMPILES the baseline arm (9.9 s measured) and spawns nothing, while the CLI entry passes in 0.36 s having compiled nothing — the integrated runner builds only the HOST-RUNNABLE spec, which applies to every cross-arch arm in the corpus. ⇒ A READER MUST NOT TAKE A GREEN WINDOWS GATE AS THIS ENTRY HAVING RUN; the legs that execute it are the Linux ones. ⚠ THE RELEASE ARM IS ALSO LEG-BOUND: an optimized arm is compiled only where its baseline arm RUNS, so on Windows it is not built at all. ⚠ COST, ✔MEASURED and stated because it is this entry's real price rather than its source size: the source is 462 bytes of code, but it emits ~2.0 MB and the compile is seconds rather than milliseconds. Figures are recorded in the lane's findings with the host and the load they were taken under; `cmake/DssTestBudgets.cmake` gives the `corpus` class its ceilings from the slowest healthy entry, so whoever folds this must re-read that tier rather than assume it. `mustDifferFromBaseline` is ✔MEASURED, not assumed: the release image differs from the baseline one byte-wise. Leg-by-leg results are NOT recorded here — whoever runs the legs writes them.
